title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: the by-name /meta read refuses an object of a disabled package (404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED), as the list and the data plane do
body:
Fixes #24097

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Implements the seat ruling on #24097 (review 6236971888: OQ1 → A, OQ2 → A, items 1–7) under the re-declared claim 6236980302.

## What changed

A disabled package's object was refused by the `/meta/objects` list and by the data plane, but `GET /meta/object/:name` still served it. Every by-name door now gives the same answer, `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`. The authoring check that needs the object still sees it.

1. **`getMetaItem`, the API face** (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`). The refusal is checked once, right after `canonicalizeMetaRequestType` and before any layer is read, so it covers the active read, `state: 'draft'` and `previewDrafts`, and the plural spelling folds into it. The refusal comes from `objectPackageDisabledError`, a constructor extracted from `assertObjectRegistered`, so the data plane and the by-name read throw byte-identical envelopes. The predicate is `registry.isObjectPackageDisabled`, optional-called through `isObjectOfDisabledPackage`, as the data plane already calls it.
2. **One private shared body.** The old `getMetaItem` body is now the private `readMetaItem`, and `getMetaItem` delegates to it after the refusal. `saveMetaItem`'s destructive-change prior read uses `readMetaItem`. There is no new public method, spec key or error code.
3. **`getMetaItemLayered`** (`?layers=true`) reads its layers without going through `getMetaItem`, so it carries the same check itself (item 5).
4. **`packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`** (cross-lane, declared to `domain:cli`). The object branch no longer falls back to `registry.getObject` when the protocol refuses `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`. The unscoped kernel's registry-first read skips an object the registry reports as disabled, so the protocol answers it. The predicate is read through a local type, because `EngineSchemaRegistryView` (`packages/spec`, outside the fence) does not declare it.
5. **`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`** (cross-lane, declared to `domain:cli`). `loadObjectItem` reads `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` as "no object" and does not log the fail-open warning. Any other thrown read still fails open and warns.

## Call sites of the by-name object read

"Today" is `origin/main` `7d6ec91d2`; "after" is this branch's head. The case is `type: 'object'` for an object whose owning package is disabled.

| Call site | What it does | Today | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| objectui `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` (`/meta/object/NAME`) | record form schema | served | 404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`. It uses the object, and the data plane already refuses its rows |
| objectui `packages/app-shell/src/providers/MetadataProvider.tsx` (`getItem('object', name)`) | console metadata cache | served | refused, same as above |
| objectui `packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx` | AI-chat handoff schema | served | refused, same as above |
| objectui `apps/console/src/pages/system/hiddenFields.ts`, `PagePreview.tsx`, `ObjectChart.tsx`, `getObjectSchema` users | render-time schema | served | refused. All of them use the object |
| objectui designer (`MetadataFieldsPage`, `PermissionMatrixEditor`, `StudioDesignSurface`, `PackageOwdOverviewPanel`) | open an object to edit | served by name, but unreachable: every entry point lists first, and `client.list('object', …)` already omits the package's objects | refused. No entry point reaches it |
| objectui `PackagesPage.tsx` (show or re-enable a package) | `/api/v1/packages` only | not a reader | unchanged |
| `protocol.ts` `saveMetaItem` destructive-change check | diffs the prior schema | served, so `409 DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` | reads `readMetaItem`, still `409 DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` (pinned; measured over HTTP below) |
| `protocol.ts` `getMetaItemCached` | REST cached item door | served | refused (an API face) |
| `protocol.ts` `applySeedBodies` adapter, build probes | seed a published package; post-publish probe | served | refused. The seed would be refused by the data plane anyway; the probes are best-effort and swallow errors |
| `packages/rest` import template / export / import-prepare | uses the object | served | refused. The import template answers `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`; the others keep their best-effort catch |
| `packages/rest` reference-label lookup (`rest-server.ts`) | label of a lookup target | served | the target's name stands in (its existing catch) |
| `packages/rest` `enforceApiAccess` → `loadObjectItem` | API-exposure gate | judged the object's `enable` | no object; the data plane answers `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, with no warning |
| `packages/runtime` dispatcher `GET /meta/object/:name` (object branch, draft read, layered read) | the door itself | served (registry first, or registry fallback) | 404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` |
| `packages/core` import runner (`servesReferenceTarget`) | is the reference target served | served | `reference_not_found` (fail-closed catch), which matches the data plane |
| `packages/services/service-automation` connector pull | uses the object | served | refused (uses it) |
| `packages/cli` ownership ceremony `lock.verdict` | lock verdict | never asked about an object (item 6, below) | unchanged; nothing in `packages/cli` is touched |

## Measurements (ruling items 5–7)

- **Item 5, `getMetaItemLayered`:** it does not route through `getMetaItem`. An ablation that removes only its own check turns its `READERS` row red ("getMetaItemLayered … → refuses": false): without the check it serves the object. Over HTTP below, `?layers=true` answers 404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`.
- **Item 6, the CLI ceremony's `lock.verdict`:** the ceremony enumerates candidates by raw SQL over `sys_metadata` (`readMetadataKeyRows`, `organization-ownership-plan.ts`), limited to `PRESENTATIONAL_TYPES` = `view, dashboard, report, translation, email_template`. The other caller, `organization-ownership-apply.ts`, asks only about `'position'`. So `lock.verdict` is never asked about an `object`, and the refusal, which is `type: 'object'` only, cannot reach it. No `needs_decision`; `packages/cli` is untouched.
- **Item 7, non-object types over HTTP** (CRM boot, below): with package `app.probe-24097` disabled, `GET /api/v1/meta/app/probe_gadget_app` answers **200** while `GET /api/v1/meta/app` omits the app (5 → 4 items). This is class (b) with that reach. It is reported to the seat to file the family card and is ⛔ not fixed here.

### HTTP readings: `pnpm dev:crm -- --fresh` at this branch's head

These come from a full `pnpm build` (76/76) and a seeded admin, against a writable package `app.probe-24097` holding object `probe_gadget` and app `probe_gadget_app`. Code-shipped `com.example.crm` refuses disable with `422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`.

| Request | enabled | disabled | re-enabled |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /meta/object/probe_gadget` | 200 | **404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`** | 200 |
| `GET /meta/object/probe_gadget?layers=true` | 200 | **404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`** | — |
| `GET /meta/object/probe_gadget?state=draft` | 404 `NO_DRAFT` | **404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`** | — |
| `GET /data/probe_gadget` | 200 | 404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` | 200 |
| `GET /meta/objects` contains it | yes (81) | no (80) | — |
| `GET /meta/app/probe_gadget_app` | 200 | **200** (item 7) | 200 |
| `GET /meta/app` contains it | yes (5) | no (4) | — |
| `PUT /meta/object/probe_gadget` dropping field `title` | — | **409 `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE`** | — |
| control `GET /meta/object/crm_account` (another package) | 200 | 200 | — |

The server log carried 0 `failing open` warnings.

## Pins

- `packages/objectql/src/package-disable-enforcement.test.ts`, the #7557 pin. `READERS` gains five `enforces: true` rows: `getMetaItem` object, `objects`, `state: 'draft'`, `previewDrafts`, and `getMetaItemLayered`. A row counts only `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` as refusing and rethrows any other error, so `NO_DRAFT` cannot pass for enforcement. The seed adds a pending draft so the draft row serves before the disable. New cases:
  - the by-name and layered refusals assert `code`, `status`, `object`, and a message identical to the data plane's;
  - the control: another package's object is still served by name and layered;
  - a field drop on a disabled package's object still answers `409 DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE`, and the stored row keeps the field.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-object-disabled-package.test.ts`, through `HttpDispatcher.dispatch`, on unscoped (registry-first) and scoped (protocol-first) kernels: 404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, `registry.getObject` never asked for the disabled name, and the control served.
- `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.object-package-disabled.test.ts`: `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` reads as no object and no warning, any other throw still warns once, and the control.
- **Pin sweep, flipped:** `packages/rest/src/rest-exposure-gate-one-object-read.test.ts`'s #24031 row "a DENIED operation answers the exposure verdict (405)" now asserts `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, with `createData` reached once. The ledger `protocol.lookup-artifact-item-call-sites.test.ts` re-keys its three by-name rows from `getMetaItem` to `readMetaItem`; the call sites, arguments and dispositions are unchanged.

## Verification (head `81e9289ba`)

- Tests: `@objectstack/objectql` 437 files / 8239 passed. `@objectstack/runtime` 409 files / 6280 passed. `@objectstack/rest` 293 files / 6016 passed. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: the first full run had 1 failure, the `lookupArtifactItem` ledger, re-keyed above. The rerun at head: 243 files / 20628 passed, 3 files skipped. Runtime rerun at head: 409 / 6280 passed.
- Typecheck: `metadata-protocol`, `objectql`, `rest` and `runtime` are clean. The runtime typecheck was rerun after the predicate typing fix.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths) derived 68 commands at `81e9289b`. All 68 exit 0. Two first refused on the shallow clone (`check-engine-split-ratio --days 90`, `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`) and passed after the deepening each prescribed. `--ran` with exit codes: "68 derived, 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)". `check-platform-checklist --changed-from origin/main`: OK, 36 anchors judged, 0 lost. Control-byte scan of the changed files: clean.
- **Ablations** (one per changed, tested behaviour). Each went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol build`, with the test resolving `dist/` through `exports`. The on-disk proof is the count of `throw objectPackageDisabledError(` in `dist/index.js`, because a comment or string marker is stripped by the bundler. A first attempt used such a marker; the preflight reported it absent from `dist/`, so it was discarded and redone.
  - (a) `getMetaItem`'s check removed: dist 3 → 2. The four `getMetaItem` rows and the envelope case went red, while `getMetaItemLayered` stayed refusing. Restored: dist 3, 12/12.
  - (b) `getMetaItemLayered`'s check removed: dist 3 → 2. Only the layered row went red. Restored: 12/12.
  - (c) the destructive-change read pointed back at `getMetaItem`: dist `await this.readMetaItem(` 1 → 0. The destructive pin went red with `expected undefined to be 'DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE'`. Restored: 12/12.
  - Each restore was proven by `blob == HEAD` and an empty `git status --porcelain`.

## Acceptance notes

- `GET /meta/:type/:name/published` (REST and the dispatcher) asks `getMetaItemLayered` inside a `try` and falls through to the published snapshot on any throw. For a disabled package's object it therefore serves the snapshot, not the refusal. It was not in the ruling's fence and was not measured over HTTP. Noted, not filed.
- The #24031 changeset (`.changeset/pre/24031-exposure-gate-one-object-read.md`, already consumed into a prerelease) says a denied operation on a disabled package's object answers the exposure verdict. This PR reverses that, and `.changeset/24097-rest-exposure-gate-disabled-package.md` states the FROM → TO. The consumed changeset is not edited.
- No changeset for `@objectstack/objectql`: its diff is a test file, which is not in its published `files`.
